items.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And so we, the horn section, which was at the time I think it was me, Chuck Findley, Ollie Mitchell, who I mentioned before, Slyde Hyde and Lew McCrury.

ctx.x: I love my work. I mean look there were sessions I did where I didn’t necessarily like — there were pop sessions we did. The ones that come to mind are the ones that we used to do with a guy named Wes Farrell, who for a brief time was married to one of Sinatra’s daughters, Tina. And he was a real, I don’t know, Mike Melvoin called him a schtarker. I guess that means sort of a poser. He was a poser. He always dressed very elegantly and had the talk — he was a fast-talking New Yorker, you know, like that, and he…
Did you ever get to the point, I’ll preface this by I was able to do an interview with Oliver Nelson Junior.

items.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023
items.q: The horn section at that time was me, Chuck Findley, Ollie Mitchell, Slyde Hyde and Lou McCurry.

ctx.x: down and do it and do my job. I think maybe that’s what this person was explaining was doing your job. Yeah you have to do your job and you have to be prepared for it. But you never know what you’re going to get. So being versatile is the answer to that. You have to be versatile. Like I mentioned earlier about Italian vibrato and mariachi vibrato. A Dixieland solo. Bebop, hard bop solo. They’re all different. But you have to be able to do all that because you never know what you’re going to get. But like I said…

I’m going to share another thing from — here’s what Tom Scott had to say about that question. And he said that he did some sessions with a producer that did The Partridge Family and David Cassidy records. And he said, “The horn section at that time was me, Chuck Findley, Ollie Mitchell, Slyde Hyde and Lou McCurry. So even if the tune was kind of dumb or mundane it didn’t matter. We were there to play the best damn horn section you’ve ever heard in your life. We took our part very seriously. We didn’t know how far…

We did that all the time. And actually Mike Melvoin wrote all those charts for that particular album. But we always, one thing I always did, always did after a session, whether it was good or bad I mean the track. I’m not talking about what we did but I’m just, like Tom said, we would make the record. We were like the icing on the cake you know. You know you build a house but you need to decorate it. We decorated it. We decorated all kinds of things you know and make it sellable, this house. You know? Because it…
